response.title: Is a solar generator enough on its own for a week-long outage, or do I still need a gas generator as backup?
response.answer:
For a week-long power outage, I'd recommend a solar generator plus a gas or dual-fuel generator as backup—unless you have a fairly large solar-and-battery system.

A solar generator can absolutely keep essential appliances running for seven days, but the biggest risk isn't battery capacity alone. It's getting enough sunlight to recharge the battery, especially during storms or several consecutive cloudy days.

What can a solar generator realistically power?

Here's an example of daily energy consumption for a household running only essential devices.

Appliance

	

Estimated daily usage




Refrigerator

	

1,200 Wh




Wi-Fi router

	

240 Wh




LED lights

	

200 Wh




Phones and laptops

	

200 Wh




Fans

	

400 Wh




Miscellaneous devices

	

200 Wh




Total

	

2,440 Wh/day

That's approximately 2.4 kWh per day, or 17.1 kWh over seven days.

The key difference is that a solar generator can recharge each day, while a battery without solar panels eventually runs out.

Three possible setups
Shop

1. Small solar generator (1–2 kWh)

Good for phones, lights, Wi-Fi, and occasional appliance use. Usually insufficient for a full week of household essentials without reliable daily solar charging.

Shop

2. Large solar generator (5–10 kWh + 1–2 kW solar panels)

Can support essential loads for a week or longer if daily solar production replenishes consumption. Multiple cloudy days remain a concern.

Shop

3. Solar generator + fuel generator

The most resilient option for a prolonged outage. Solar handles everyday loads quietly, while the fuel generator recharges batteries when sunlight is insufficient.

Why cloudy weather matters so much

Suppose you have a 5 kWh battery, 1,000 W of solar panels, and daily consumption of 2.4 kWh.

Simplified model: starts with a full 5 kWh usable battery, assumes constant daily sunlight and 75% effective solar yield. Does not model appliance startup surges or hourly charging.

Adjust the sliders to see how cloudy days or increased power consumption affect the battery. A zero reading means the battery would have run out by that day.

When I'd skip the gas generator

A solar-only system is reasonable if you have enough battery storage for at least 2–3 days of essential loads, enough solar panels to recharge during less-than-ideal conditions, and no critical need for high-power appliances such as central air conditioning or electric heating.

For a seven-day outage, a hybrid setup is generally the safer choice. If using a fuel generator, operate it outdoors at least 20 feet from doors, windows, and vents, never in a garage, and use carbon monoxide alarms.

One question that changes my recommendation

Essentials + air conditioning or heating
Most of the house, including major appliances
Calculate my recommended setup

That will help determine whether you need a $1,000–$2,000 portable backup solution or a substantially larger system.
